messages.subject: Re: DEB simulations for males?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mike,

I have tried simulating the "male strategy" by using the default values for abclutch, which makes individuals "lay eggs" as soon as they have energy lay 5 eggs -- since the species lays clutches of 300-600 eggs, that happens very often, and they depleat the repro buffer every year. Then, I multiply the number of eggs by E_0, and I interpret those Joules as the energy used for spermatogenesis, courtship behavious, and all other reproductive behavious (similar to what you said in a previous email). Does it make sense? Or is it something fundamentally wrong with my approximation?

Thanks!

Urtzi

On Friday, July 31, 2026 at 5:22:57 AM UTC+2 NicheMapR wrote:
> Hi Urtzi,
> It uses E_0 - energy in an egg - plus the clutch size to work out when to empty the buffer so we'd need ideally a new parameter for energy of a sperm to make it work for males but you could just specify a "clutch size" and E_0 for sperm and I think it will work, only the wetmass calc of an embryo stage might look a bit odd because it uses the energy of an egg in the calculation.
> All the best,
> Mike
>
> On Sunday, July 19, 2026 at 4:07:04 AM UTC+10 urtzi enriquez wrote:
> > Hi Mike,
> >
> > I am now making some simulations for males and females, using male specific parameters (in fact, individual level parameters) as you suggested.
> >
> > The problem is that the "reproductive strategy" is the same for females/males (using batch=1 and abclutch), so the males don't use the energy stored in the reproduction buffer some years because they are unable to produce a clutch... However, I would expect males to deplete the reproduction buffer each year, fertilizing more or less eggs, depending on how much energy they have stored. Is it possible to simulate that?

messages.subject: Re: DEB simulations for males?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Urtzi,

The DEB model is always allocating energy to reproduction (p_R) after "puberty" according to the kappa rule. So, if you don't have a different kappa parameter for males, or kappa_R, then for a male it's the energy flow to sperm biomass. The buffer handling rules, i.e. the "abclutch" or clutch size, just controls how it is packaged and dispensed to the environment which is not part of DEB theory formalism, DEB just gives you the flow. And yes you could consider other reproductive activities as being paid for by p_R than just sperm production but note that if those things are dissipative (e.g. locomotion), then it would represent heat loss rather than biomass dispensed to the environment. In short, yes what you are doing makes sense but the code is assuming it's producing and releasing biomass (eggs) so the mass will be changing accordingly with biophysical consequences since the mass is coupled to the heat budget. You could change kappa_R to make it so more of the energy to reproduction is dissipated if you are counting locomotion as part of the male's reproductive spend, in which case some of that biomass accumulation would instead become heat production.

All the best,
Mike
